title: Mississippi AI Laws

reading.body:
Mississippi's two AI-related laws are a definition and an education bill, not regulation: the state has defined artificial intelligence without restricting it.

HB1723 defines "artificial intelligence" for use in the Mississippi Code and imposes no duties, restrictions, or penalties. SB2294 is an education law that adds artificial intelligence concepts to a computer science graduation requirement, alongside math, reading, financial literacy, and civics initiatives. The only operative AI content in either law is a definition and a curriculum requirement.

For AI specifically, this means Mississippi has taken no position on how AI systems are built, deployed, or held accountable. The definition in HB1723 is groundwork that a later law could attach obligations to, but nothing in this data does so. The education provisions matter for the future workforce, not for the compute, buildings, or power that constrain AI scaling today.

What this data does not cover is any Mississippi law that regulates AI use, procurement, or development, because none appears here. It also does not say whether such bills were introduced and failed, or whether more are pending. Two laws, one definitional and one educational, is the whole of what the state has enacted on this record.

Mississippi has enacted 2 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Mississippi

2 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • SB2294: Education; institute initiatives to promote literacy in math, reading, finance, computer science, and civics. passed 2026-04-08

    This law establishes several education initiatives in Mississippi: the Mississippi Math Act creating the Moving Mathematics in Mississippi (M3) program for K-12 math coaching, K-5 screening, algebra readiness indicators, and professional development; literacy proficiency requirements for grades 4-8 including individual reading plans, interventions, and parent notification; a financial literacy graduation requirement; a computer science graduation requirement including artificial intelligence concepts; and mandatory civics instruction in grades 8-12. It also creates a Moving Mathematics in Mississippi Fund and requires annual reporting.

  • HB1723: Artificial intelligence; define. passed 2026-03-09

    This act defines the term 'artificial intelligence' for use in the Mississippi Code. It does not impose any duties, restrictions, or penalties.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Mississippi. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
